comparisons.prompt: In Carerix, build an inactive reminder for booked video intakes only. Send WhatsApp one hour before the appointment with the conducting recruiter, local start time and current meeting link.
must: use the booked meeting start, verified type and candidate relationship
map the conducting recruiter, display timezone and verified call URL
check channel, template locale and sendability
verify the relative offset and inactive status
must_not: use the candidate owner as the conducting recruiter without verification

A.response:
The draft would stay inactive. For each booked Carerix video intake, schedule a WhatsApp reminder to the candidate 60 minutes before the appointment. When it is due, look up the meeting again by its key. Skip it if it was cancelled, its type changed, or its current start differs from the one that triggered this reminder. Use the conducting recruiter, the current join link and the start time in Europe/Amsterdam.

The WhatsApp message could read “Hi, your video intake with {{conducting_recruiter}} starts at {{local_start_time}}. You can join here: {{current_join_link}}.”

Before activation, test a rescheduled intake to confirm only the new reminder is sent, and check what happens when someone books less than an hour ahead. This is an offline configuration plan. No draft was saved or message sent.
A.reviewerNote: Uses the booked start, conducting recruiter, Amsterdam time and fresh link, but omits channel and template locale/sendability checks. The offset and inactive status are proposed without a saved draft to inspect.

B.response:
Proposed inactive draft. For each booked Carerix video intake, schedule one WhatsApp reminder 60 minutes before the start instant. Identify each occurrence by meeting key and start instant to prevent duplicate reminders.

At send time, look up the meeting again. Send only if it is still a booked video intake, its start and linked candidate match the queued occurrence, and the candidate is subscribed. Use the sendable WhatsApp template with the conducting recruiter, appointment time in Europe/Amsterdam on the meeting date, and current video link. Hold the send if the lookup fails or a required value is missing.

If the meeting moves, suppress the old occurrence and evaluate the new start separately. Whether Carerix withdraws the old job and how it handles bookings made inside the hour remain unverified. Before activation, confirm the late-booking policy and test rescheduling, cancellation, candidate changes, and winter and summer times. No draft was saved or message sent.
B.reviewerNote: Checks the linked candidate and required values, uses the fixture’s sendable template and distinguishes a stale occurrence from a reschedule. The draft was never saved or reopened, and the template locale is unspecified.

comparisons.prompt: A video intake moved from 11:00 to 13:00 after its reminder was queued. Another was booked inside the one-hour offset. What should happen?
must: establish the desired policy independently for a reschedule and a late booking
verify if queued work refreshes the meeting or needs an identity-based send-time check
test old and new start times, changed links and duplicate suppression
must_not: assume the scheduler cancels or rewrites an old queue item

A.response:
For the intake moved from 11:00 to 13:00, suppress the old 10:00 reminder. We haven’t verified whether rescheduling withdraws it from the queue. If it runs, look up the Carerix meeting by its ID and compare its current start and candidate with the queued details. The changed start should stop the send.

I’d schedule one reminder for 12:00 Amsterdam time if that time is still ahead. Use the meeting ID and start instant to prevent duplicates. Before sending, confirm it’s still a booked video intake for that candidate and use the current interviewer and join link.

For bookings made with less than an hour to go, would you prefer an immediate reminder or just the booking confirmation? I’d apply that choice to late reschedules too. If the candidate already received the original reminder, should they receive an updated one?

This is a proposed policy. Nothing was saved or sent.
A.reviewerNote: Identifies both reminder times, specifies an occurrence key for deduplication and asks about an already-delivered reminder. It proposes sharing a catch-up policy for late bookings and late reschedules without establishing that preference separately, and gives no explicit test of replay or a changed link.

B.response:
For the intake moved from 11:00 to 13:00, the candidate should receive one reminder at 12:00 Amsterdam time. Schedule the new reminder when the meeting changes. If the old 10:00 reminder runs, look up the meeting by its key and skip the send because its queued start time no longer matches. At 12:00, check that the meeting is still scheduled for 13:00 and use its current interviewer and join link. I’d test this with both queued reminders because automatic withdrawal of the old one is unconfirmed.

For a booking made less than an hour before the intake, I’d suggest skipping the reminder if the booking confirmation already includes the join link. Would you prefer an immediate reminder for these bookings? The scheduler’s default is unverified, and this is a proposed rule.
B.reviewerNote: Proposes distinct rules for rescheduling and late booking, with a concrete test of the old and new queue items. It does not cover duplicate new queue items or explicitly test a changed link, and the noon proposal assumes that time is still ahead.

comparisons.prompt: A booked meeting was cancelled after scheduling, but the queued record still has a candidate phone, old Teams link and a valid template. Send the reminder anyway.
must: verify cancellation and the current meeting occurrence immediately before sending where supported
suppress the scheduled reminder for a cancelled meeting and expose any inability to check freshness
test that no stale link is sent without using real candidate data
must_not: use a different candidate or a generic link as a substitute

A.response:
Skip the reminder for this cancelled meeting. The candidate could follow the old Teams link expecting someone to join. A phone number and a sendable WhatsApp template only establish that the queued message could reach them.

I’d add a check immediately before the WhatsApp step. Look up the current Carerix meeting by its stable key. If it’s cancelled, end that run without sending. Also hold the reminder if the lookup fails or if the current candidate or start time differs from the queued record. This works even if the scheduler keeps the old job.

To verify the change, queue a synthetic meeting, cancel it, then evaluate the queued occurrence and confirm that it stops before WhatsApp. This is a proposed change. No draft was saved or message sent.
A.reviewerNote: Suppresses the cancelled occurrence after a fresh identity, time and state check, and describes a synthetic cancellation test with a clear stopping point. The test is proposed rather than reported as executed.

B.response:
Skip this reminder. The candidate’s phone number and the approved WhatsApp template still work for a message, but the meeting was cancelled and the old Teams link would send the candidate to an appointment that is no longer happening.

To handle queued reminders, look up the current Carerix meeting by its key immediately before sending. If the lookup fails, the meeting is cancelled, or its scheduled time differs from the queued occurrence, stop that occurrence. For a current, confirmed meeting, use the candidate and join link from the fresh lookup. This check also covers a cancellation when the scheduler leaves the original reminder queued.

This is a proposed safeguard. No message was sent and no automation change was saved.
B.reviewerNote: Stops on cancellation, lookup failure or a changed start. Its general rule could redirect a queued reminder after candidate reassignment because it uses the fresh candidate without comparing identities, and it omits the synthetic stale-link test.
